content: Before using streptomycin injection, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (such as tobramycin or gentamicin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Streptomycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG or typhoid vaccine. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using streptomycin, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has directed you to take low doses of aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams a day), continue to take the aspirin as directed. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, lab and/or medical tests (such as kidney function, hearing tests, and streptomycin blood levels) should be performed regularly to monitor your progress and reduce the risk of side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. Store unmixed medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used in combination with other medications to treat active tuberculosis (TB) infections, particularly if you cannot take other TB drugs or if you have a drug-resistant form of TB. Streptomycin belongs to a class of drugs known as aminoglycoside antibiotics. This medication is administered by injection, usually into a muscle, as directed by your doctor. When starting TB treatment, it is typically given once daily or as directed. It is important to rotate the injection site daily to avoid skin problems. The dosage is based on the type of infection, your weight, medical condition, streptomycin blood levels, and response to treatment. If you are administering this medication at home, learn all preparation and usage instructions from your healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. TB treatment with this medication usually lasts for 9 months or longer. After receiving streptomycin daily for 1 to 2 months, your doctor may reduce the frequency to 2-3 times a week. Your doctor may also direct you to stop using this medication before discontinuing other TB medications. Do not stop taking this medication (or other TB medicines/antibiotics) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor. Skipping or changing your dose without approval may worsen side effects or make the infection (especially TB) more difficult to treat due to resistance. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or loss of appetite. Pain, irritation, or redness may occur at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. This medication can sometimes cause serious nerve damage, potentially resulting in permanent hearing loss and balance problems. The risk is higher if you have kidney disease, are receiving high doses of this medication, use it for a long time, are older than 60 years, or become severely dehydrated. To reduce the risk of dehydration, drink plenty of fluids while using this medication unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Your doctor will monitor your progress to minimize the risk of these side effects and may test your hearing, kidney function, and streptomycin blood levels. Before undergoing surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using this medication. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
